description: Register a standing deal watch. Writes the intent to the sourcing pipeline and returns delivery channels: a one-time token-gated Atom feed plus an optional webhook that activates after interpretation. Progress and live matches are available through check_watch using the returned watch_id. Structured scope/taxonomy/criteria use deterministic staging when intent is omitted; supplied prose requires interpretation and family intents can require review. conditions defaults to new and open_box. To follow a partner publisher instead, pass publisher (a slug from GET /v1/publishers) with any optional criteria: the follow is active at once, delivers only that partner's deals, and sources nothing.

agent_id.description: Self-identifier for telemetry (e.g. "claude-desktop:tom"). Helps us prioritize agent demand.

brands.description: Required brands, any-of. exact_model and product_line require one brand. Publisher follows can use this as a filter without sourcing.

conditions.description: Accepted deal conditions. Defaults to new + open_box. During consent, surface all four categories and ask whether to add refurbished/pre_owned or restrict to new only.

exclude_terms.description: Words or short phrases a matching deal title must NOT contain, e.g. ["heatsink", "bundle"]. Literal, case-insensitive. Pass this when the human names things to exclude. Use specs for capacity or size and conditions for condition, not this. If omitted, explicit "exclude ..." or "without ..." wording in the intent is registered instead; effective_filters.exclude_terms in the response shows exactly what was registered.

feed.description: Create a private Atom feed (default true).

intent.description: Free-text intent (e.g. "Oura Ring 4 silver under $350"). The interpretation pipeline owns the structuring. Required for legacy free-text registration. Optional with explicit structured scope; when provided it still requires interpretation. On a publisher follow, omit it on a follow (it is rejected there, since a follow has no interpreter).

max_price_cents.description: Hard price ceiling for delivery, in cents (a numeric string like "150000" is accepted).

min_discount_pct.description: Minimum reported discount_pct for delivery, using each deal's own reference (listed amount, MSRP, tracked street price or observed average). Not a retailer-list-only filter or historical-low guarantee. A stricter basis requirement is unsupported; keep it explicit rather than silently omitting it.

model_number.description: Manufacturer model number (MPN) for the exact variant — e.g. "K-65XR70" for the Sony BRAVIA 7 65". With exact_model scope, one brand and taxonomy_id, this is requester-supplied identity: deterministic staging does not check product existence. Conflicting identities and family-level intents require review.

product_name.description: Product-line name, required only for product_line. exact_model uses brand + MPN; put other material requirements in specs or executable intent.

publisher.description: Follow a partner publisher by slug (list: GET /v1/publishers). Delivers only that partner's deals, filtered only by the structured criteria you pass (specs, conditions, max_price_cents, min_discount_pct, exclude_terms, taxonomy); do not send intent. Active immediately; nothing is sourced. Unknown or paused partners are an error.

scope.description: Explicit requested scope. With taxonomy_id and structured criteria, omit intent to use deterministic staging. A publisher follow can use category scope as a delivery filter only.

specs.description: Structured spec/attribute constraints. Omit keys you have no value for. Whole-entry null, empty, none and n/a markers are ignored and counted. Pass these whenever the human names a hard requirement. Every supported key, with its type, operators, enum values, unit and accepted unit conversions, is listed at https://api.kitsdeals.com/v1/spec-keys (generated from the registry this deployment serves; read it before choosing a key). Shapes: numeric <spec_key>_min/_max (an exact 8 TB drive is storage_gb_min: 8000 plus storage_gb_max: 8000), enum/list <spec_key>_in for any-of (camera_type_in, bundle_includes_in), enum-list <spec_key>_contains_all for every requested member (bundle_includes_contains_all), and boolean direct keys (bundle). Numeric bounds may use {value,unit} with a registered conversion. Storage uses decimal GB: 1 TB = 1000 GB. Unknown keys are rejected; deals missing the constrained spec are excluded (must-have semantics). Deterministic intent extraction is a fallback; explicit specs always override it, and soft phrasing ("around 65 inches") is never auto-constrained.

taxonomy.description: Publisher follows only: narrow the partner's deals to a Google Product Taxonomy node, by id or path (e.g. "Electronics > Computers"). A filter, never a sourcing target.

taxonomy_id.description: Canonical taxonomy id from watch_options, including intentional parent scopes (descendants match). Supported across the complete taxonomy.

unresolved_requirements.description: Material requirements not represented by supported fields. Preparation refuses these explicitly; never omit them to obtain activation.

webhook_callback_url.description: https:// endpoint to receive push deliveries (activates post-interpretation).

name: register_watch
title: Register a deal watch
